newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises to 11.9 vs 11.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises to 11.9 vs 11.2 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose 70 basis points to 11.9 percent on Wednesday on stronger term lending, dealers said.
The daily trade totalled 60.1 million kuna against a 103 million kuna supply.
Call money loans granted at a steady 10.5 percent accounted for roughly two thirds of the 35.4 million kuna fresh trade.
Two-month interbank deals were granted at a higher 19 percent rate.
Insurers rolled over one-week loans at an unchanged nine percent and one-moth deals at 13.5 percent.
Banks renewed call money deals at 10.5 and 13 percent, five-day interbank borrowings at 12 percent, one-week funds at 10 and 11 percent and one-month loans at 15 and 16 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna mid-rates for Thursday weaker at 6.0825 against the dollar and firmer at 3.5714 against the German mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
